The filing of an FTC Identity Theft Report legally establishes that I am disputing this account as fraud and identity theft, not as a billing disagreement. 

The FTC Identity Theft Report provides legal standing under federal law, including the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ) and the Fair and Accurate Credit Transactions Act ( FACTA ), which require creditors and credit reporting agencies to block and remove fraudulent information once identity theft has been properly reported.

2. Provide evidence of the original signed agreements, payment records, and verification documents supporting the accuracy of the accounts.

3. If Navy Federal can not provide verifiable documentation within the FCRAs timeframe, delete the unverifiable accounts from all credit bureaus immediately. 
4. Confirm in writing that corrective action has been completed.

- FCRA 1681i ( a ) : Consumers have the right to dispute and have unverifiable data removed within 30 days.

- FCRA 1681s-2 ( b ) : Furnishers must investigate disputes received from credit bureaus.

- FDCPA 807 : Prohibits the use of false, deceptive, or misleading representations in the collection or reporting of debts. 
Summary I have made good faith attempts to resolve this matter directly through the credit bureaus. The bank 's failure to detect altered instruments at the point of deposit was a direct and proximate contributing cause of my total financial loss. A denial built on a misclassified transaction is not a valid denial it is evidence that no proper investigation occurred. Four accounts were originally enrolled in the program : XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX I made my first payment into the program on XX/XX/XXXX. According to GRT Financials records, two accounts were settled : XXXX XXXX ( original enrolled balance : {$23000.00} ) XXXX XXXX XXXX ( original enrolled balance : {$10000.00} ) The total original enrolled balance of these two settled accounts was {$34000.00}. On XX/XX/XXXX, I received a written summary from a GRT Financial supervisor providing a breakdown of fees collected, creditor payments made, and other program activity. The financial figures referenced in this complaint are derived from that written summary and information contained in my client portal. GRT Financial provided a written summary stating that : Total amount paid into the program : {$8500.00} Settlement fees collected : {$4600.00} Total paid to creditors : {$2000.00} Remaining settlement fees claimed by GRT Financial : {$4900.00} GRT Financial later provided information indicating that settlement fees assessed on the two settled accounts totaled approximately {$9500.00}. Based on GRT Financials own records, {$4600.00} in settlement fees were collected in less than XXXX year while only {$2000.00} was paid to creditors during that same period. I am requesting a review of whether this fee collection structure complies with the FTC Telemarketing Sales Rule ( TSR ) and any other applicable consumer protection laws and regulations. In addition, I requested written explanations regarding my account on XX/XX/XXXX, XX/XX/XXXX, XX/XX/XXXX, XX/XX/XXXX, and XX/XX/XXXX. In these communications, I requested : The mathematical calculation used to determine my current payment amount ; The effective date of any payment adjustment resulting from the removal of accounts from the program ; An explanation of why my payment amount remained approximately {$890.00} per month after two of the four enrolled accounts were removed from the program ; A detailed calculation showing how settlement fees were determined, calculated, and earned. Although GRT Financial subsequently provided additional account summaries, fee totals, payment schedules, and general explanations regarding my program, it did not provide the specific calculations and methodologies I requested. GRT Financial informed me that after two of the four enrolled accounts were removed from the program, my monthly payment would remain approximately {$840.00} per month after the removal of the XXXX XXXX fee and that my projected program completion date would be accelerated from approximately XX/XX/XXXX to approximately XX/XX/XXXX. I am seeking clarification regarding the contractual, mathematical, and regulatory basis for maintaining approximately the same monthly payment while accelerating the projected completion date from approximately XX/XX/XXXX to approximately XX/XX/XXXX. I do not understand how the removal of two of the four enrolled accounts resulted in a reduction of the projected program duration of approximately 15 months while maintaining approximately the same monthly payment, and I have not been provided sufficient calculations to independently verify that determination. Furthermore, on XX/XX/XXXX, I spoke with a GRT Financial escalation specialist regarding these issues. During that conversation, I was informed for the first time that GRT Financial had accelerated my projected program completion date from approximately XX/XX/XXXX to approximately XX/XX/XXXX. Prior to that conversation, I had not been notified that my projected program completion date had been materially changed. I did not receive a telephone call, email, written notice, contract amendment, or other documentation informing me of this change before it was implemented. I also was not provided with a detailed calculation or explanation supporting the basis for the change. In addition, although GRT Financial informed me that my projected completion date had been accelerated to approximately XX/XX/XXXX, my online client portal continues to display scheduled ACH drafts extending into XXXX. I have not received a written explanation reconciling these two representations. As a result, I remain unable to determine my actual projected program completion date or independently verify the accuracy of the information being provided regarding my account. As of the date of this complaint, I still have not received : A complete mathematical calculation showing how my current payment amount was determined ; The numerical calculation supporting the decision to maintain approximately the same monthly payment after the removal of two enrolled accounts ; The contractual basis for accelerating my projected program completion date from approximately XX/XX/XXXX to approximately XX/XX/XXXX ; The formula, percentages, and methodology used to calculate settlement fees ; The basis upon which settlement fees were deemed earned ; The calculation supporting GRT Financials claim that additional settlement fees remain due. I am particularly concerned that less than XXXX year after enrollment, GRT Financial had collected {$4600.00} in settlement fees while only {$2000.00} had been paid to creditors. Despite repeated written requests, I have been unable to obtain sufficient documentation to independently verify how these fees were calculated, earned, and collected or to determine whether the fee collection structure complies with applicable law. I am also concerned that one of my creditors ultimately filed a lawsuit while I was enrolled in the program and making regular payments into the program. Although I attempted to resolve that matter independently by sending settlement proposals to the creditors attorneys, I remain concerned about the relationship between the programs fee collection structure and the amount of money that was ultimately paid to creditors. As a result of that lawsuit, the court filing became publicly available through court records and was subsequently indexed by third-party websites and internet search engines. This has caused me significant professional concern and has negatively affected my reputation. I respectfully request that the CFPB consider this as part of its review when evaluating whether GRT Financials fee collection practices and administration of my account complied with applicable consumer protection laws and regulations. I respectfully request that GRT Financial provide : A complete written accounting of all fees assessed ; The calculations used to determine those fees ; The basis upon which those fees were deemed earned ; The calculations supporting my payment amount ; The contractual basis for maintaining approximately the same payment amount while accelerating the projected completion date of the program ; An explanation of how its fee collection practices comply with applicable federal consumer protection laws and regulations. If the CFPB determines that GRT Financial improperly assessed or collected fees or otherwise failed to comply with applicable consumer protection laws or regulations, I respectfully request that appropriate relief be considered, including reimbursement of any fees determined to have been improperly assessed or collected. Thank you for your review of this matter.

Earlier that same day, XXXX XXXX had already obtained a signed buyer 's order from XXXX XXXX, with her designated as the buyer of the vehicle. That document exists and is in my possession. It proves that XXXX XXXX knew the correct party designations before I ever walked through the door. The reversal of roles on the final printed contract was not a clerical error. It was a deliberate, premeditated act. III. Additional Deceptive Practices Beyond the fraudulent role assignment, the following deceptive acts were committed against us at the point of sale : XXXX XXXX failed to provide a Buyer 's Guide for the vehicle as required by the FTC Used Car Rule ( 16 C.F.R. Part 455 ). We never received this document. The tire protection contract for {$1100.00} was signed by me, not XXXX XXXX, despite the vehicle being sold to ( as XXXX XXXX represented ) XXXX XXXX as buyer. This contract was also signed under false pretenses. XXXX XXXX 's salesperson, XXXX XXXX, verbally represented that the dealership had inspected the vehicle and certified it was free of known issues. The check engine light activated within XXXX hours after purchase, and the dealership subsequently acknowledged they could reset the light so it would not be visible, indicating they were aware of the vehicle 's condition prior to sale. IV. The Formal Rescission Upon discovering that the printed contract had fraudulently designated me as the primary buyer, contrary to all representations made to me, we formally exercised our right to rescind the contract. Under Texas common law, a contract obtained through fraudulent misrepresentation is voidable by the defrauded party. Under the Texas Deceptive Trade Practices Act, Tex. Bus. & Com. Code 17.50, rescission is an available remedy when fraud or misrepresentation has been used to sign a contract. Our rescission letter was sent via certified mail. XXXX XXXX deliberately refused to sign for their copy of the certified mail. However, the rescission was simultaneously transmitted to XXXX XXXX representative XXXX XXXX XXXX via email. This established actual written notice to XXXX XXXX regardless of their deliberate refusal to accept certified delivery. Under Texas law, deliberate refusal of certified mail does not defeat legal notice. When XXXX failed to honor the initial rescission, we sent a Final Demand for Immediate Rescission of Contract via certified mail. XXXX / GM Financial received and signed for this final demand on XX/XX/XXXX, as confirmed by XXXX tracking documentation. XXXX therefore had written notice of our demand for rescission on XXXX separate occasions, XX/XX/XXXX and XX/XX/XXXX, and failed to act on either. V. We subsequently sent a Final Demand for Immediate Rescission of Contract, which XXXX received on XX/XX/XXXX. XXXX failed to honor this second demand as well. This position is legally untenable. Complaint Against : U.S. Department of Education and its federal student loan servicers Issue Summary : Failure to process legally authorized loan discharges, misrepresentation of Public Service Loan Forgiveness ( PSLF ) eligibility, and unlawful obstruction of Income-Driven Repayment ( IDR ) access, resulting in financial harm and inaccurate credit reporting.

I am submitting this complaint regarding systemic violations by the U.S. Department of Education ( ED ) and its loan servicers related to borrower protections guaranteed under federal law.

1. Failure to Properly Discharge Loans for Defrauded Borrowers I attended a for-profit college that engaged in fraudulent and deceptive practices. Borrowers from this institution were misled regarding job placement rates, program accreditation, transferability of credits, and post-graduation outcomes. These actions qualify for borrower defense to repayment and/or group discharge under federal law.

Despite eligibility for discharge, ED and/or its servicers failed to timely process the discharge, continued collection activity, and continued to report the loans to credit reporting agencies. This resulted in financial harm and credit damage despite statutory entitlement to relief.

2. Misrepresentation of Public Service Loan Forgiveness ( PSLF ) Eligibility ED and its servicers provided inaccurate and misleading information regarding PSLF eligibility. Borrowers were told their loans or repayment plans qualified when they did not, or were discouraged from enrolling in qualifying repayment plans. In other cases, borrowers were incorrectly informed that qualifying employment or payments did not count.

These misrepresentations caused borrowers to lose qualifying payments, delay forgiveness, and incur unnecessary interest and fees, in violation of federal consumer protection standards.

3. Removal of IDR Application Forms and Unlawful Processing Halts ED unlawfully removed Income-Driven Repayment ( IDR ) application forms from its website and/or servicer platforms, halted IDR processing, and failed to provide alternative access. This directly prevented borrowers from enrolling in or recertifying affordable repayment plans required by federal law.

As a result : Borrowers were pushed into delinquency or default Affordable monthly payment options were denied Negative credit reporting occurred despite borrowers attempting to comply These actions violate federal statutes governing student loan servicing and repayment access, including requirements to provide IDR options and process applications in a timely manner.

4. Credit Reporting Violations Loans that should have been discharged, placed in administrative forbearance, or enrolled in IDR were inaccurately reported as delinquent or in default. This violates the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ), which requires information to be accurate, complete, and not misleading.

Harm Suffered : Denial of legally entitled loan discharge Loss of PSLF qualifying time Inability to access affordable repayment plans Accrued interest and fees Damaged credit reports Emotional and financial distress Requested Resolution : I respectfully request that the CFPB require the U.S. Department of Education and its servicers to : Immediately process all applicable loan discharges for defrauded borrowers Correct PSLF records and restore lost qualifying payments Restore and properly process all IDR applications and recertifications Remove all inaccurate negative credit reporting related to these violations Cease unlawful servicing practices that obstruct borrower access to federal protections

Sub-issue: Denied request to lower payments
Consumer complaint narrative: Consumer Financial Protection Bureau Complaint I am requesting the CFPB investigate what I believe to be a predatory auto loan and unfair lending practices related to my vehicle financing. I believe I was placed into a loan that was designed to keep me in debt while financing a vehicle that was worth substantially less than what I was charged. The vehicle is a XXXX XXXX XXXX, financed through Credit Acceptance after being purchased from XXXX XXXX. From the beginning, this transaction was financially unreasonable. The vehicle 's advertised purchase price was approximately {$11000.00}, yet after warranties, fees, and financed add-ons, my total financed amount exceeded {$16000.00}. I also made a {$2000.00} down payment, yet despite making payments for approximately three years, my loan balance barely decreased and, in some periods, actually increased because nearly every payment was applied to interest instead of principal. The interest rate on my loan is approximately 20.5 %, which is extraordinarily high considering the age and value of the vehicle. I believe I was placed into a loan that the lender knew would be nearly impossible to repay. To make matters worse, the vehicle has now suffered catastrophic mechanical failures, including : - Engine failure - Water pump failure - Failed catalytic converters The vehicle is no longer drivable. Despite the vehicle becoming unusable, I continued making payments in an effort to protect my credit. However, my balance has continued increasing daily due to interest. My balance increased from approximately {$8600.00} to over {$8800.00} even while I was attempting to remain current. I have now paid thousands of dollars toward this loan and still owe nearly the same amount as years ago. This demonstrates that the structure of this loan primarily benefited the lender while leaving me with almost no equity despite years of payments. I also believe I was sold products and add-ons that did not provide meaningful value, including warranties and other financed products that significantly increased my loan amount. These products dramatically inflated the amount financed beyond the actual value of the vehicle. Because of the vehicle 's age, mileage, high interest rate, and loan balance, refinancing has been impossible. I have effectively been trapped in this loan. I have contacted both the dealership and the finance company seeking assistance, including requesting settlement options or reasonable alternatives due to the catastrophic mechanical failure. Instead of offering meaningful assistance, I was essentially told no reasonable options were available. The result is that I have paid thousands of dollars for a vehicle that is now worthless, while still owing thousands more. I believe this is the exact type of lending practice that consumer protection laws are intended to prevent. I respectfully ask the CFPB to investigate whether the lender and dealership engaged in unfair, deceptive, or abusive acts or practices, including but not limited to : - Financing a vehicle for substantially more than its actual market value. - Structuring a loan with an excessively high interest rate that prevented meaningful reduction of the principal balance. - Financing warranties and additional products that significantly inflated the loan amount. - Failing to ensure the loan was reasonably affordable. - Leaving me trapped in negative equity with no realistic ability to refinance or escape the loan. - Refusing to provide reasonable loss mitigation or settlement options after the vehicle suffered catastrophic mechanical failure. As a consumer, I believe I was set up for financial failure rather than successful repayment. I respectfully request that the CFPB require the lender to fully review this account and provide appropriate relief, including : - A complete audit and accounting of all payments made and how they were applied. - Investigation into whether the financed amount exceeded the vehicle 's true market value. - Review of all financed add-on products and warranties. - Elimination or substantial reduction of the remaining balance. - Correction of any negative credit reporting related to this account while the dispute is under investigation. - Any additional relief the CFPB determines is appropriate after reviewing the facts. I entered this loan believing I was purchasing reliable transportation. Instead, I have spent years paying mostly interest on a vehicle that is now inoperable, while remaining burdened by thousands of dollars in debt. I respectfully request your assistance in investigating these lending practices and providing appropriate consumer protection. The lender and dealership have repeatedly responded to my concerns by stating, in essence, " You signed the contract, '' implying that my signature alone excuses every aspect of this transaction. I strongly disagree. A consumer 's signature should not shield a lender or dealership from scrutiny if the transaction itself was structured in a way that was unfair, deceptive, or financially devastating. Simply obtaining a signature does not relieve a financial institution of its responsibility to conduct business fairly or to ensure consumers fully understand the true financial consequences of the loan they are entering. No reasonable consumer, had they genuinely understood that they would pay thousands of dollars over several years while barely reducing the principal balance, owe substantially more than the vehicle 's actual value, become trapped in a loan that could not realistically be refinanced, and still owe thousands of dollars after the vehicle became mechanically worthless, would knowingly agree to those terms. The dealership 's position appears to be that because paperwork was signed, no further responsibility exists. They have even pointed to language stating that I understood I could not later rescind or challenge the agreement. I believe this ignores the larger issue. Consumer protection laws exist because a signature alone does not automatically make a transaction fair or lawful. If that were true, there would be no purpose for laws prohibiting unfair, deceptive, or abusive acts or practices. My complaint is not that I signed paperwork. My complaint is that I believe I was placed into a loan that was designed to benefit the lender regardless of whether I could realistically succeed financially. The structure of this loan, the excessive interest rate, the inflated financed amount, the financed add-on products, and the fact that years of payments resulted in almost no reduction of my principal created an outcome that I could not reasonably have understood or anticipated. I respectfully ask that this complaint be evaluated based on the fairness of the transaction itselfnot solely on the existence of my signature. A signature should reflect informed consent, not serve as a blanket waiver of a consumer 's right to challenge lending practices that may have been unfair, deceptive, or abusive.

STATEMENT OF FACTS AND LEGAL VIOLATIONS Payment Made and Account Standing On or about XX/XX/XXXX, the Complainant, XXXX XXXX, paid the remaining balance owed on his secured credit account in the amount of {$260.00} to Defendant Self Financial , Inc. ( Self ). This account is a secured credit line, funded by the Complainants own money, and was established for the express purpose of building credit. 
Improper Rejection of Lawful Payment Method Despite the payment being valid and lawful, Self failed to properly recognize or process the Complainants primary bank account. As a direct result of Selfs failure, the Complainant was forced to use a secondary payment method. The Complainant informed Self that this was the only bank account available to him, as all attempts to open additional bank accounts had been denied. 
Notice of Federal Law Violations The Complainant explicitly informed Self that denying or mishandling lawful payments on a secured credit account, and threatening adverse action as a result, constituted violations of federal consumer protection laws, including but not limited to : Truth in Lending Act ( TILA ), 15 U.S.C. 1601 et seq., which requires accurate account administration and prohibits unfair or deceptive practices involving credit accounts ; Electronic Fund Transfer Act ( EFTA ), 15 U.S.C. 1693 et seq., which protects consumers from improper handling of electronic payments ; Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ), 15 U.S.C. 1681 et seq., which prohibits furnishing inaccurate or misleading information and requires reasonable procedures to assure maximum possible accuracy ; Unfair, Deceptive, or Abusive Acts or Practices ( UDAAP ) under 12 U.S.C. 5531, enforced by the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau ( CFPB ).

The Complainant further demanded that his secured payment be properly credited within XXXX hours, warning that failure to do so would constitute a willful violation of federal law. 
Improper Account Closure and False Attribution On or about XX/XX/XXXX, Self unilaterally closed the Complainants secured credit account, citing an alleged statement that the Complainant had requested closure during a prior telephone call on XXXX. This allegation is categorically false. 
At no time did the Complainant : Request account closure ; Provide written authorization to close the account ; Consent to termination of the secured credit line. 
Selfs own policies require verification and confirmation prior to closing a consumer credit account. No such verification occurred. 
Retaliation and Bad Faith The closure occurred immediately after the Complainant asserted his legal rights and objected to federal law violations. The timing and circumstances demonstrate retaliation, bad faith, and willful misconduct, particularly given that the account was secured by the Complainants own funds. 
Frustration expressed by the Complainant during the call was a direct result of Defendants unlawful conduct and does not constitute consent to account termination. 
LEGAL VIOLATIONS Federal Law Violations Truth in Lending Act ( 15 U.S.C. 1605, 1638 ) Improper administration and termination of a secured credit account without authorization or proper disclosure.

Electronic Fund Transfer Act ( 15 U.S.C. 1693f ) Failure to properly process and investigate electronic payments.

Fair Credit Reporting Act ( 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ) Furnishing or causing inaccurate account status information and failing to follow reasonable procedures.

CFPB UDAAP Provisions ( 12 U.S.C. 5531 & 5536 ) Retaliatory account closure, misrepresentation, and abusive conduct. 
State Law Violations ( Generally Applicable ) Breach of Contract Breach of the Covenant of Good Faith and Fair Dealing Conversion of Secured Funds Negligent and/or Intentional Misrepresentation Consumer Protection Act Violations ( state-specific ) SUPPORTING CASE LAW ( Illustrative ) Johnson v. MBNA America Bank, N.A. , 357 F.3d 426 ( 4th Cir. 2004 ) Creditors must conduct reasonable investigations and may not rely on false internal assertions.

Safeco Ins. Co. v. Burr, 551 U.S. 47 ( 2007 ) Willful violations include reckless disregard of statutory duties.

Spokeo , Inc. v. Robins, 578 U.S. 330 ( 2016 ) Inaccurate credit handling constitutes concrete consumer harm.

In re Sanchez, 941 F.3d 625 ( 2d Cir. 2019 ) Retaliatory conduct following assertion of statutory rights is actionable. 
SUMMARY Defendant Self Financial , Inc. unlawfully mishandled a secured payment, retaliated against the Complainant for asserting federally protected rights, falsely attributed consent to close the account, and terminated a secured credit line without authorization, in violation of federal and state law.

Under Section 611 of the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( 15 U.S.C. 1681i ), has a legal obligation to conduct a reasonable reinvestigation whenever a consumer disputes the completeness or accuracy of information contained in a credit report. This obligation requires more than simply accepting a furnisher 's response without conducting a meaningful review of the disputed information. A reasonable reinvestigation includes verifying the accuracy of the reported information directly with the furnisher and carefully evaluating whether the information being reported complies with the requirements of federal law. Additionally, Section 607 ( b ) of the Fair Credit Reporting Act requires consumer reporting agencies to follow reasonable procedures to assure the maximum possible accuracy of all information included in consumer reports. Section 623 of the Fair Credit Reporting Act further requires furnishers of information to provide complete and accurate information to consumer reporting agencies and to properly investigate disputed information submitted through a credit reporting agency.

Consumer complaint narrative: In XX/XX/XXXX, I received a phone call from my loan lender stating that my student loans were nearing repayment status and that my monthly payments would increase. At that time, I did not fully understand the total balance of my loans, as I had been led to believe by a family member that the loans were being managed and paid. During this period, I took over full financial responsibility for these loans and have remained prompt and diligent with all required payments. As I began managing the loans independently, I reasonably relied on information provided directly by representatives of the loan lender when making significant financial decisions. On XX/XX/XXXX, I made a large payment of approximately {$39000.00} toward my student loans. Before making this payment, I spoke with a loan lender representative who explained that once XXXX loan was paid off, my remaining loans would be eligible for reamortization. During this same call, the representative explicitly stated that my loans would be automatically reamortized as a result of this payment and that the new payment amount would be reflected within approximately XXXX days. I was instructed to call back only if I did not see the change. The reamortization did not occur. On XX/XX/XXXX, I contacted the loan lender to follow up. I was informed that the previous representative had provided incorrect information, but I was told that reamortization could still be processed upon request and that it would reduce my monthly payment. I specifically asked when the change would take effect and was told to make my normal XXXX payment, with the new payment reflecting in XX/XX/XXXX. As of the XX/XX/XXXX billing cycle, no reamortization had occurred, and my monthly payment remained unchanged. I made multiple attempts to resolve this issue : On XX/XX/XXXX, I was told the loan lender could not reamortize my loans because I had only paid off XXXX loan, and that payments across all XXXX loans were required, a criterion that had never previously been disclosed. I requested that a formal case be opened, that prior calls be reviewed, and that corrective adjustments be applied. A case number was issued. On XX/XX/XXXX, my case was escalated due to no response. This material information was disclosed only after I questioned it directly. The manager also stated that the loan lender does not reamortize student loans at all, contradicting previous representations. I also requested access to call recordings and was informed that they could only be obtained through a subpoena. As a result of this situation, I have experienced significant financial burden and mental distress. I took over full financial responsibility for these loans in good faith and have remained current and prompt on my payments. However, I made a {$39000.00} payment in reliance on explicit representations that my loans would be reamortized and that my monthly payment would decrease. Instead, I have faced prolonged uncertainty, repeated misinformation, ongoing higher monthly payments, and continued interest accrual. This has materially impacted my ability to responsibly manage my finances and move forward with my life, including delaying my ability to refinance and achieve financial stability. This contradiction demonstrates a lack of accuracy and reliability in the servicers handling of the loan. I immediately disputed this action in writing, clearly stating that XXXX XXXX is not part of the mortgage and should not be included in escrow. To date, the servicer has not provided any documentation demonstrating authority to include this parcel or justification for its actions. This issue is not isolated. It is part of a broader pattern of conduct that includes : Misrepresentation of loan terms and structure Failure to apply credits and payments properly Inflation of loan amounts and payoff figures Improper inclusion of property not subject to the mortgage Ongoing inaccurate servicing and escrow practices Despite repeated disputes and requests for clarification, the servicer continues to act in a manner that increases my financial burden and creates confusion regarding what property secures the loan. This ongoing conduct is causing harm and uncertainty, particularly as it relates to the scope of the mortgage lien, the accuracy of the loan balance, and the handling of escrow funds. Given that this matter is already under active litigation, I am requesting that your agency : XXXX. Conduct a formal review of the loan servicing practices in this matter XXXX. XXXXXX/XX/XXXXXXXX Pennsylvania Recording Statute Under Pennsylvania law, any interest in real property, including a mortgage, must be in writing, properly recorded, and applies only to the property specifically described in the recorded instrument. Accordingly, a mortgage can not be expanded verbally or administratively to include additional property. A servicer can not treat a parcel as collateral unless it is expressly included in the written mortgage agreement. XXXX. Established Pennsylvania Mortgage Law It is a fundamental principle of mortgage law that a lien attaches only to the property specifically described in the mortgage. If a parcel is not included in the legal description, it is not collateral for the loan and can not be treated as such. XXXX. Pennsylvania Unfair Trade Practices and Consumer Protection Law (XX/XX/XXXX) ( XXXXXX/XX/XXXXet seq. ) This law prohibits deceptive practices, misrepresentation, and unfair conduct in business. Where a servicer represents that only XXXX parcel is encumbered but later treats an additional parcel as collateral, such conduct raises concerns of misrepresentation and deceptive servicing practices. XXXX. Improper Loan Servicing Practices While mortgage servicing is also governed by federal law, Pennsylvania law recognizes that improper handling of escrow accounts, payments, and property designation may constitute unfair or deceptive practices. The inclusion of property not subject to the mortgage, along with inaccurate escrow handling, raises serious concerns regarding the accuracy and legality of the servicers actions.

Onity disregarded the 60 month structure, re-spread my escrow shortage over 12 months and then 24 months, raised my monthly payment by over {$500.00}, received my contractual payment and refused to apply it, and began treating me as in default. Onity has refused to identify any legal authority for disregarding the 60 month term. What Onity 's own documents show My VASP modification set my monthly payment at {$2300.00} beginning XX/XX/XXXX. The interest rate is 2.5 %. Principal and interest is {$1400.00}. The escrow shortage of {$6900.00} was structured to be repaid over 60 months and was already built into that monthly payment. New misconduct : Onity reported my payment as late to the credit bureaus On or about XX/XX/XXXX, the same day it sent the Early Intervention notice, Onity furnished information to XXXX or more consumer reporting agencies reporting my XX/XX/XXXX mortgage payment as late or delinquent. This violates the Fair Credit Reporting Act. Consumer complaint narrative:
Dear CFPB, I paid the outstanding balance on my Bank of America credit card # XXXX in full on XX/XX/year>, thereby satisfying the amount due as reflected on the statement and in accordance with the cardmember agreement. 

Subsequent to payoff, Bank of America assessed additional residual or trailing interest that was not disclosed at the time of payment and was not reasonably ascertainable from the balance presented for payoff. 

Under the cardmember agreement and applicable disclosure requirements, interest terms must be clear, conspicuous, and accurately reflected when a consumer tenders payment in full. The assessment of post-payment interest without contemporaneous disclosure creates ambiguity as to the amount required to fully satisfy the obligation. 

During a telephone call with Bank of America, I was advised that in order to obtain a true payoff amount, I was required to call and request a final or total balance. This requirement is not disclosed in the cardmember agreement or otherwise presented to the consumer at the time of payment. 

As a result, a consumer may reasonably believe the obligation has been fully satisfied, while additional interest continues to accrue in an indeterminate amount. This creates a situation where the account is paid in full in practice, yet remains open to further charges without a clearly disclosed payoff figure. 

The lack of a clear, contractually disclosed payoff mechanism renders the remaining balance ambiguous and functionally unknowable at the time of payment, particularly where interest continues to compound on accrued interest. 

I am disputing this charge and requesting a credit of the residual interest, along with written confirmation that the account reflects a true XXXX balance and that no further interest will accrue.

Consumer complaint narrative: I am requesting the complete deletion of Bank of Americas reporting of an alleged {$11000.00} balance because the account is legally timebarred under Florida Statute 95.11 ( 2 ) ( b ). Bank of America ( or its servicer/collector ) continues to report this timebarred balance as if it is valid and enforceable. Reporting a legally unenforceable debt without disclosing its timebarred status is misleading, deceptive, and violates the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ). -- - Legal Basis Supporting Deletion 1. Florida Attorney General Unfair & Deceptive Practices The Florida Attorney General has repeatedly stated that : Attempting to collect or imply enforceability of a timebarred debt is deceptive, Failing to disclose the timebarred status misleads consumers, and Collectors must not misrepresent the legal status of a debt under the Florida Deceptive and Unfair Trade Practices Act ( FDUTPA ), Fla. Stat. 501.204. The AG has taken enforcement actions where creditors or collectors misrepresented the enforceability of timebarred debts or failed to disclose that a debt could not legally be sued on. Bank of Americas reporting of a full active balance without acknowledging the debts timebarred status is inconsistent with Florida AG guidance and enforcement precedent. -- - 2. The current letter simply states the balance without any supporting documentation. -- - Requested CFPB Action DELETION ONLY Because the debt is timebarred, legally unenforceable, and unsupported by documentation, I am requesting that CFPB require Bank of America to DELETE the tradeline entirely. Deletion is the only appropriate remedy because : The debt can not be collected The debt can not be enforced The reporting is misleading The reporting is incomplete The reporting is inaccurate under FCRA The furnisher has not validated the balance The furnisher has not acknowledged the timebarred status The Florida Attorney General considers misrepresenting timebarred debts a deceptive practice If Bank of America can not validate the enforceability and accuracy of the {$11000.00} balance, the tradeline must be removed.

Product : Auto loan Company : JPMorgan Chase Bank , N.A . ( Chase Auto ) Complaint Narrative I am submitting this complaint regarding improper servicing of my auto loan following a total loss and the resulting inaccurate credit reporting. 

Timeline of events : On XX/XX/XXXX, my vehicle was declared a total loss and was surrendered to my insurance company. 
On XXXX XX/XX/XXXX, the insurance company issued payment for the vehicles market value. 
The GAP claim was initiated in LATE XXXX / EARLY XX/XX/XXXX because I was required to first obtain final refund documentation related to extended warranty and ancillary products from the original dealership. 
The dealership significantly delayed issuing these refunds and the associated paperwork, despite my repeated follow-ups. 
I initiated the GAP claim immediately after the lender confirmed receipt of the extended warranty refund and all required documentation became available. 
I did not delay the GAP claim voluntarily ; the timing was dictated by documentation requirements outside of my control. 
On early XX/XX/XXXX, I initiated a GAP insurance claim immediately after all final insurance payments were received. 
On XXXX XX/XX/XXXX, I received written confirmation from the GAP administrator stating that the remaining loan balance was paid in full and that I had no remaining financial obligation. 

GAP Approval and Subsequent Conflicting Information from Lender After receiving written confirmation from the GAP insurance provider indicating that, based on the GAP Breakdown / Worksheet, the remaining loan balance would be fully satisfied and that I would not owe any further payments to the lender, I reasonably understood the matter to be resolved. 
Relying on this information, I believed the loan was effectively closed, with the remaining balance to be paid directly by the GAP provider. 

Subsequently, after contacting the lender for clarification, I was informed that I was still considered to have an outstanding balance, as the lender had not yet received the GAP Breakdown / Worksheet and certain GAP-related refunds. 
I was instructed by the lender to request that the GAP insurance provider send the required documentation directly to Chase. 

I contacted the GAP insurance provider and requested that the GAP Worksheet be sent to my loan holder. On [ XX/XX/XXXX ], I received written notification from the GAP provider stating that they were unable to successfully reach Chase and suggested arranging a conference call. 

Due to repeated difficulties coordinating communication between the lender and the GAP provider, I contacted Chase again and was advised that I could submit the required document via fax. 

I submitted the GAP Breakdown / Worksheet via fax in XXXX XXXX, using the submission method provided by the lender. 

In early XX/XX/XXXX, I contacted Chase to confirm receipt. At that time, Chase confirmed that all required refunds had been received, but stated that the GAP Worksheet submission was still under review. 

As of today, despite submitting the required documentation in XXXX and following up multiple times, no updates or account changes have been made, and the case remains pending without resolution. 

Despite the above, my account was not placed in an insurance or GAP pending status. Instead, it was later reported as charged off, while the insurance and GAP resolution process was ongoing. 





Additional Context / Consumer Position I reasonably relied on written confirmation from the GAP administrator stating that the loan was settled in full. Based on this official documentation, I had a good-faith belief that no further payments were due. 

At no point did Chase provide clear written instructions advising me to continue making payments while the insurance and GAP claim were pending, nor did Chase communicate that failure to do so could result in a charge-off.

Given the extensive delays and repeated communication failures between the lender and the GAP provider, I have a reasonable belief that even if I had continued making payments during this period, there was no guarantee that those payments would have been properly credited or refunded. The remaining loan balance at the time was relatively small after my insurance paid vehicle 's market value ( remaining balance was approximately {$2200.00} ), yet the account was handled as if I owed a substantially larger sum, ultimately resulting in a charge-off being reported. 
The charge-off and resulting credit reporting appear to be the direct result of servicing and processing failures, not a refusal to pay or abandonment of the loan. 

Additionally, the original dealership significantly delayed the process, as all required refunds related to extended warranty and ancillary products had to be processed through them before the GAP claim could be initiated. Despite my repeated follow-ups, these delays were outside of my control and directly impacted the timing of the GAP claim.

Impact on Consumer Throughout this entire process, I made consistent and good-faith efforts to communicate with the lender and kept them informed of all developments, including the total loss determination, insurance payments, and the status of the GAP claim. Despite this, my account continued to be marked as delinquent, with each payment reported as missed, without consideration of the ongoing insurance and GAP resolution.

As a result of this handling, the account was ultimately charged off. At the time, due to my lack of prior experience with auto loans, total loss claims, and U.S. credit reporting practices, I mistakenly believed that a charge-off indicated that the loan had been settled or closed. Once I later learned that a charge-off represents a serious negative credit event, I immediately began taking steps to dispute the status and provide the requested documentation. 
As a result of the above, my credit report reflects a charge-off that has caused significant and disproportionate damage to my credit profile, despite the loan being covered by insurance and GAP.

This was my first auto loan and first total loss, and I had no prior experience with insurance and GAP claim processing. Based on the vehicle being surrendered, insurance payments being issued to the lender, and written confirmation from the GAP administrator that the loan was settled, I held a reasonable belief that no further payments were required while the claims were being finalized.

Resolution Requested I am requesting the following : 1. Expedited review and final resolution of the insurance and GAP payoff ; 2. A written explanation detailing why my account was charged off while a total loss insurance and GAP claim were pending ; 3. Correction of all credit bureau reporting related to this account to reflect the accurate status following insurance and GAP payoff ; 4. Written confirmation of the current loan balance, which should reflect {$0.00} if all payments have been properly applied.

In prior correspondence DATED XX/XX/year> PennyMac acknowledged that the following amounts are owed to me : {$300.00} related to a State Farm insurance payment that I paid out of pocket, which should have been covered through escrow. {$750.00}, which was separately identified and acknowledged as an outstanding balance owed to me. In its response da, the company introduced a new and inconsistent position regarding the {$750.00}, claiming that the funds were credited to my escrow account and/or that a payment had been issued and subsequently returned. I do not accept this claim. I have never received any such payment. My address on file is correct, and there is no valid reason for any alleged return. PennyMac has failed to provide any supporting documentation, including proof of mailing, tracking information, delivery confirmation, or evidence of return. Without such documentation, this claim is unsubstantiated and does not constitute fulfillment of their obligation. If a payment was in fact issued and returned, the company must provide verifiable evidence and immediately reissue the payment. Furthermore, even if a check had been issued and returned, PennyMacs unilateral decision to apply those funds to my escrow account is unacceptable and improper. Once the company has acknowledged that the funds are owed directly to me, those funds must be disbursed to me, not retained, redirected, or internally reallocated at the companys discretion. Any alleged return of a mailed check does not extinguish their obligation to pay me directly. Instead, they are required to promptly reissue the payment. Crediting funds to an escrow account does not constitute a disbursement to the borrower and does not satisfy the obligation owed to me. Under the Real Estate Settlement Procedures Act ( RESPA ), 12 U.S.C. 2605, and its implementing regulation, Regulation X ( 12 C.F.R. I am submitting this complaint to dispute the actions of a debt collection agency, Credit Collection Services, for violations of the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( FDCPA ) and the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ). 

On XX/XX/year>, I received a collection notice from Credit Collection Services by mail for the first time regarding an alleged debt. 

On XX/XX/year>, within the XXXX validation period provided under federal law, I mailed a written debt validation request to Credit Collection Services XXXX 

Credit Collection Services failed to respond to my debt validation request and did not provide any verification or documentation substantiating the alleged debt. 

Instead, after receiving my validation request, the company reported the collection account to the credit reporting agencies without first validating the debt. 

Violations of Federal Law Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( FDCPA ) 15 U.S.C. 1692g ( b ) Under the FDCPA, once a consumer timely disputes a debt and requests validation, a debt collector must cease all collection activity until the debt has been properly verified. Reporting a disputed debt to the credit bureaus constitutes continued collection activity. By adding this account to my credit report without first validating the debt, Credit Collection Services violated this provision.

Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ) 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ( a ) & ( b ) The FCRA requires furnishers of information to ensure that information reported to consumer reporting agencies is accurate and verified. Furnishing an unverified and disputed debt to the credit bureaus is inaccurate and misleading. Additionally, failing to note the account as disputed further violates the FCRA. 

Harm Caused to My Credit Profile The improper reporting of this unverified collection account has caused, and continues to cause, harm to my credit profile, including but not limited to : Potential and actual credit score reduction Increased difficulty obtaining credit, housing, or favorable interest rates Damage to my overall creditworthiness and financial reputation Emotional distress resulting from inaccurate and unlawful credit reporting This harm is especially concerning given that the debt was timely disputed and never validated as required by law.

By failing to produce records proving compliance with 1666b, Capital One is effectively acknowledging that these late payment notations are unsupported and unlawful. Reporting such derogatory information to the credit bureaus without proper validation not only violates TILA 1666b, but also constitutes inaccurate reporting under the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ( b ) ), which requires furnishers to ensure maximum possible accuracy when reporting consumer information.

The continued reporting of inaccurate account statuses and late reporting indicators after a previous dispute requires additional review to ensure that the information maintained in my credit file is accurate and that proper procedures are being followed. Once a transaction has been declined, it should not be processed again without explicit consumer re-authorization. Allowing resubmission and approval after a decline particularly for customers unenrolled from overdraft services undermines Regulation E protections and constitutes a failure of the banks authorization controls. 

3. Posting Order and Transparency Issues Wells Fargos own letter acknowledges that deposits and debits may post in unpredictable order depending on merchant submission. When combined with continued overdraft coverage after unenrollment, this creates systemic unpredictability that exposes consumers to fees they could not reasonably avoid.

Provide a complete transaction audit ( including timestamps of authorization and settlement ) for all overdraft events from XX/XX/year> to XX/XX/year>, with the exception of the {$100.00} that Wells Fargo refunded in XXXX. They would only refund 3 overdraft charges, and I have had 57 ( fifty-seven ) overdraft fees deducted from my account ; 54 remaining.

Refund {$2000.00} in fees resulting from these improper overdraft events. 

Confirm in writing that my account is now fully excluded from all overdraft services and that no negative marks will be reported during the investigation. 

5. Regulatory and Compliance Concerns Given Wells Fargos history of enforcement actions related to overdraft practices, this matter raises broader questions about ongoing compliance with CFPB and OCC orders. I respectfully request that the CFPB review this case for potential systemic issues affecting other consumers who have opted out yet continue to experience similar overdraft activity. 

Conclusion I appreciate your attention to this matter and request a written response confirming receipt and reopening of the case. I will provide additional transaction details or screenshots upon request. 

Thank you for your commitment to transparency and consumer fairness. 

Sincerely, XXXX XXXX XXXX

This is a clear violation of the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ) and the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( FDCPA ). 


-- - SUMMARY OF THE PROBLEM LVNV Funding LLC reported a collection account on my credit report with no prior notification, no proof, no validation, and no documentation showing : What the debt is for Who the original creditor is Whether the debt is legally mine Whether LVNV owns the debt Any signed agreement with my signature I have never had any account, loan, credit card, or service with LVNV Funding LLC or their alleged original creditor. 
This account is fraudulent, unverified, and illegally reported.

-- - LEGAL VIOLATIONS 1. FDCPA 809 ( 15 U.S.C. 1692g ) Failure to Provide Validation of Debt A debt collector must provide written validation of the debt including : The name of the original creditor, Proof of the debt amount, Proof that the debt is owed by me, And a copy of the original signed contract.

LVNV failed to provide ANY of this.

-- - 2. FDCPA 807 False or Misleading Representations LVNV is attempting to collect a debt I do not owe. 
Reporting a collection without verification is false, deceptive, and illegal.

-- - 3. FDCPA 808 Unfair Collection Practices Continuing to report or pursue a debt without proof is an unfair practice.

-- - 4. FCRA 602 & 607 Right to Accurate Reporting LVNV is reporting inaccurate information.

Under FCRA 607, they must ensure maximum possible accuracy.

They have not done so.

-- - 5. FCRA 611 Failure to Reinvestigate After disputing the account with the credit bureaus, LVNV continued to verify it without providing : A contract A signature Any documentation This violates FCRA 611, which requires proper reinvestigation.

-- - 6. UDAAP Unfair, Deceptive, Abusive Acts or Practices LVNV : Reported a debt I do not owe Provided no validation Continued collection activity Used false and misleading credit reporting This is a UDAAP violation under CFPB authority.

Sub-issue: Confusing or misleading advertising or marketing
Consumer complaint narrative:
We purchased a new car on XX/XX/year> and at the time of sale the car still had an open recall within the NHTSA database and within the manufacture database which against federal law. The dealership insists that their paperwork excludes them from complying with the law that the recall has to be completed in the vin database at the time of sale not later. They keep insisting their paperwork supersedes the law and they have time for it to update. They refuse to rescind the sale as request

ed Under federal law ( 49 U.S.C. 30120 ( i ) ), a dealer may not sell or lease a new vehicle subject to an open recall unless the defect is remedied before delivery. Selling the vehicle while the recall is still open constitutes a violation of federal law. Under federal regulation ( 49 C.F.R. 573.15 ), manufacturers must report complet
ed recall repairs to NHTSA, and the VIN database is the official, legally recognized record of whether a recall is remedied. Until the database reflects the repair, the vehicle is legally considered unrepaired.

In North Carolina, misrepresenting a recall as completed when it remains open may also constitute an Unfair and Deceptive Trade Practice under N.C. Gen. Stat. 75-1.1, exposing the dealer to potential treble damages.

Until this is done in the official system of record ( NHTSA ), the vehicle can not legally be treated as repaired or safe for delivery under federal law.

IV. Nature of the XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX and XXXX XXXX require me to deposit my own money before making purchases. The amount I deposit varies from month to month. Consequently, my available spending amount changes each billing cycle, my reported balances fluctuate according to my deposits, and I can not spend beyond the amount of my own deposited funds. These products function differently from traditional revolving credit cards. V. Concern Regarding the Underwriting Process I attempted to explain the nature of these deposit-backed credit builder accounts and requested that my application receive individualized consideration. I am concerned that my explanatory correspondence and supporting information were not meaningfully considered, that the underwriting process relied primarily on automated decision-making, and that the underwriting system may have interpreted my deposit-backed accounts as traditional revolving credit accounts without distinguishing their unique structure. Requested Relief I respectfully request that the CFPB ask LightStream to review my application through an individualized manual underwriting process, consider the unique characteristics of deposit-backed credit builder accounts, explain how the adverse action reasons were determined in light of my credit profile, confirm whether my supporting correspondence and documentation were reviewed, and take any corrective action deemed appropriate if deficiencies in the underwriting process are identified. Forcing the consumer to resell tickets for an event that was cancelled at XXXX is an unfair and deceptive business practice. Likewise, requiring repayment for a loan tied to an undelivered product constitutes an unlawful attempt to enforce a contract without consideration. 

In summary, I purchased a valid product for a specific date and time. n after transferring servicing but failed to responsibly address origination-era insurance and subsidy inquiries.

This situation began due to a military administrative error. My spouse was serving a 12-month unaccompanied rotation in XXXX XXXX , and I moved with our young son to XXXX  to be near family for support. Before these orders, we fully expected to return to our XXXX  home, so many of our belongings remained there packed. We owned two XXXX  properties at the time. The home financed by Freedom Mortgage was rented out through a property manager and generating rental income. The second Tennessee home was occupied by my brother, who remained there after XXXX to maintain the property and prevent vacancy issues. 

At the same time, we were also paying for the XXXX  home where my son and I lived. Because the military failed for nearly eight months to update my spouses XXXX from XXXX  rates to the higher XXXX  rate, we were underpaid by approximately {$1800.00} per month. Even with rental income and family assistance, we were forced to juggle funds between three homes. We never fell 30 days behind on the XXXX  home, but we often paid just before the 30-day mark. We expected the military to correct the XXXX  quickly, but instead, the error persisted until mid-summer, when my spouse finally received approximately {$17000.00} in backpay. This hardship was caused entirely by a documented military pay error, not borrower negligence. 

During this period, I contacted Freedom Mortgage to explain the situation. A representative told me I qualified for forbearance, but gave no explanation of what that meant, no terms, no disclosures, and did not tell me that forbearance requires a signed agreement. The only document I received was an Eligibility for Informal Forbearance letter, which stated that if I did not respond by XX/XX/year>, the offer would be deemed rejected. I never accepted or signed anything, and I continued making monthly payments. I do not know when Freedom Mortgage began treating my loan as if it were in forbearance because I was never provided any dates or confirmation. Throughout the entire period they later labeled as a forbearance, I continued paying before reaching 30 days late. Once the military corrected my spouses pay, I immediately brought the loan current and have remained current ever since. 

Despite this, Freedom Mortgage coded my account internally as being in forbearance and reported this false status to the credit bureaus. This is inaccurate and violates mortgage servicing rules and FCRA accuracy requirements. An unaccepted and unsigned informal hardship offer should never be reported as an actual forbearance plan. 

Freedom Mortgage also reported inconsistent and contradictory delinquency information to the bureaus. They initially reported two 30-day late payments, which automatically disqualifies a borrower from obtaining a VA mortgage for at least 12 months. After multiple disputes, they corrected only one bureau to show one 30-day late payment and informed me verbally that the forbearance never existed. However, two bureaus still show two 30-day lates, XXXX still shows one, and the forbearance remark remains on multiple reports. Even a single 30-day late within the last 12 months may cause denial depending on lender overlays, and a forbearance status results in automatic denial across mortgage programs. These inconsistencies have left me unable to qualify for any mortgage or many rentals. 

When my spouse unexpectedly received XXXX  orders to North Carolina, we had no housing lined up. We were unable to qualify for off-post rentals or mortgage approval due to the inaccurate reporting. As a result, my spouse, my five-year-old son, and I were forced to live in a hotel for over a week and a half with all of our belongings in storage. We eventually moved into on-post housingthe only unit available at the time. While suitable for many families, this unit is significantly smaller than our previous homes and can not accommodate our belongings. We brought approximately 70 % of our major furniture, but almost all of our non-furniture items ( including most kitchen supplies, household goods, and personal belongings ) remain stored off-post due to lack of space. The kitchen and storage areas are too small, requiring us to use the dining room and one spare bedroom almost entirely as storage. Only the living room, kitchen, and two bedrooms are fully functional. This transitional, partially unpacked state is not a long-term solution and is a direct result of Freedom Mortgages inaccurate reporting.

I have contacted Freedom Mortgage multiple times to request written proof that my account is not in forbearance, since the credit bureaus continue to report it. Each time, representatives told me that they had submitted a request for the documentation to be emailed to me or uploaded to my borrower portal. Nothing was ever provided. When I followed up after waiting several days or a week, I was given different explanations each time. This has gone on for over a month. Only within the last several days did a representative finally tell me that there is no forbearance code on my account and no history of any forbearance ever being applied. Yet, even after this admission, no documentation was provided and the reporting has not been corrected. Multiple credit bureaus continue to show an active forbearance status that Freedom Mortgage now admits should not exist.

These errors have displaced my family, caused significant financial and emotional hardship, and continue to prevent us from securing permanent housing. I am requesting that the CFPB require Freedom Mortgage to : 1. Remove the inaccurate forbearance remark from all credit bureaus.

2. Remove all inaccurately reported 30-day late payments tied to the military XXXX  error and the false forbearance. 
3. Provide written confirmation that no forbearance was ever placed on the account.

4. Correct and synchronize all reporting across all bureaus.

5. Provide documentation of all corrections to me and my loan officer so we can secure permanent housing.

Freedom Mortgage has had numerous opportunities to correct these errors but has repeatedly failed to do so. CFPB intervention is urgently needed.

She did not disclose that Chase would charge off my account after receiving only the first settlement payment, nor did she inform me of any adverse credit reporting consequences tied to the settlement process. Chase reported the account as charged off on XX/XX/XXXX only 127 days after my last regular payment of XX/XX/XXXX. This charge-off occurred while I was actively making payments under the settlement agreement. On XX/XX/XXXX, I submitted a formal written dispute to Chases Executive Office/Customer Advocacy department , specifically citing XXXX XXXX XXXX and requesting correction of the premature charge-off designation. On XX/XX/XXXX, Chase responded with a form letter ( XXXX ) stating that our reporting of your account is accurate and that no updates or corrections are needed. Chase provided no regulatory citation, no policy explanation, and no written justification for deviating from the 180-day charge-off standard, despite my explicit written request for one. II. BASES FOR THIS COMPLAINT A. Violation of OCC XXXX XXXX : Premature Charge-Off OCC Bulletin 2000-20 establishes that national banks are required to charge off open-end credit accounts ( including credit cards ) at 180 days past due, not earlier, unless extraordinary circumstances exist. My account was charged off on XX/XX/XXXX, only 127 days after my last regular payment of XX/XX/XXXX. This is 53 days earlier than the minimum 180-day delinquency threshold required under OCC guidance . Chase has not identified any extraordinary circumstance justifying an early charge-off. In fact, there was no extraordinary circumstance I was actively making settlement payments at the time Chase reported the charge-off. Charging off an account while a consumer is in an active payment arrangement, without disclosure and without regulatory justification, is an unfair and deceptive practice. B. Violation of the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ), 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ( b ) Under the FCRA, furnishers of information ( such as Chase ) have a duty to investigate disputes and correct or delete inaccurate information. I provided Chase with a specific, documented dispute citing the exact regulatory basis for inaccuracy. Rather than conducting a meaningful investigation, Chase responded with a boilerplate letter asserting accuracy without substantive analysis, without regulatory citation, and without addressing the 180-day charge-off rule at all. This constitutes a failure to properly investigate and correct inaccurate reporting as required by 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ( b ). C. Unfair, Deceptive, or Abusive Act or Practice ( UDAAP ) Under the Dodd-Frank Act Chases conduct constitutes an unfair and deceptive practice under 12 U.S.C. 5531. Specifically : A Chase representative made an oral representation at account settlement that the account would report as paid as settled, without disclosing that a charge-off had already occurred or was imminent. This misrepresentation was material I relied on it when agreeing to the settlement terms. Chase charged off the account prematurely, mid-settlement, causing significant harm to my creditworthiness and credit score. Chases refusal to correct the reporting without even addressing the regulatory argument I raised compounds the deceptive nature of its initial conduct. III. HARM SUFFERED Significant damage to my credit score due to the premature charge-off designation, which is more damaging than a paid as settled notation. Reputational harm and reduced access to credit and financial services. Numerous emails seeking clarification and requesting a substantive explanation for the delays either went unanswered or received no meaningful response. Instead, I now find myself XXXX day away from foreclosure after more than a year of cooperation, despite having a qualified buyer and complying with every request made by First Home. Consumer complaint narrative: I am submitting this complaint to request a formal investigation into inaccurate and unverified collection accounts currently being reported on my credit file. The companies involved are XXXX XXXX XXXX, which has reported a collection account to XXXX, and Southwest Credit Systems, which has reported a collection account to XXXX. Both accounts appear to be reporting the same balance of {$290.00}. I do not recognize this alleged debt and have never entered into any contractual agreement with Southwest Credit Systems or XXXX XXXX XXXX. I have never signed any contract or agreement with either of these third-party collection agencies that would create a legal obligation for me to pay them directly. The companies mentioned are : XXXX XXXX XXXX ( reported to XXXX XXXX Southwest Credit Systems ( reported to XXXX ) Often this happens when a single original debt gets sold or assigned to multiple collectors, or when one collector re-ages or reassigns the account. If two collectors are reporting the same debt simultaneously, that can potentially violate the Fair Credit Reporting Act. I am requesting full validation of the alleged account, including documentation identifying the original creditor, the complete account history, proof of assignment or transfer of the alleged debt, and documentation demonstrating that I have a legal obligation to pay this debt. Additionally, I have discovered that another collection agency is reporting the same balance on my credit file, which raises serious concerns about the accuracy and validity of this account. Furthermore, under the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( 15 U.S.C. 1692g ), a consumer has the right to request validation of an alleged debt, and a debt collector must provide proper verification before continuing collection activities. Because I do not recognize this debt and have no contractual agreement with either collection agency, the reporting of this account without proper validation may constitute inaccurate or unverified reporting to consumer reporting agencies. If Southwest Credit Systems or XXXX XXXX XXXX can not provide sufficient documentation proving the validity of this debt, the identity of the original creditor, and their legal authority to collect and report this account, I request that the account be immediately removed from all consumer reporting agencies, including XXXX XXXX, and XXXX. Consumer complaint narrative:
I formally disagree with the response provided by Goldman Sachs Bank USA ( the Bank ) and submit this feedback to document ongoing inaccuracies, failures to comply with federal consumer protection laws, and unresolved identity theft issues related to an Apple Card account that I do not own, did not authorize, and did not benefit from. 

This feedback is submitted in connection with CFPB complaint number XXXX, which the Bank requested be closed with explanation. Because the Bank failed to properly address the substance of my dispute, I am also initiating a new CFPB complaint to ensure continued regulatory review of this matter. 

I. ACCOUNT OWNERSHIP IS EXPRESSLY DISPUTED The Banks response repeatedly asserts that I am liable for the account and that I electronically consented to the Apple Card Customer Agreement. I unequivocally dispute this characterization. 

I do not own this account, did not authorize its opening, did not authorize the charges or activity reported, and did not receive the benefit of any transactions associated with the account. Assertions of electronic consent alone do not establish that I was the individual who applied for, opened, or used the account. In cases of identity theft, reliance on automated application records without corroborating identity verification is insufficient. 

The Banks response does not demonstrate that it conducted a reasonable investigation into whether the account activity was authorized by me, nor does it provide evidence that the account was not the result of identity theft. 

XXXX. FTC IDENTITY THEFT REPORT FILED I have filed an Identity Theft Report with the Federal Trade Commission ( FTC ) stating that the Apple Card account issued by Goldman Sachs Bank USA and the associated activity were not authorized by me. 

This is a material and legally significant fact that the Bank failed to meaningfully address. Under federal law, including the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ), once a consumer submits an identity theft report, furnishers have heightened obligations to : Conduct a reasonable and thorough investigation Cease furnishing information resulting from identity theft Block or correct inaccurate credit reporting related to identity theft The Banks response does not explain how it satisfied these obligations after receiving notice of identity theft. Merely asserting that no internal error occurred does not meet the standard required by law.

III. FAILURE TO COMPLY WITH FCRA OBLIGATIONS The Banks response conflates alleged contractual liability with its independent legal duties as a furnisher of information to consumer reporting agencies. These are distinct issues. 

Even if a financial institution claims a contractual relationship exists, it remains legally obligated to ensure that any information furnished to credit reporting agencies is accurate, complete, verifiable, and legally reportable, especially when identity theft has been alleged and documented. 

The Bank did not provide evidence demonstrating that the account was opened or used by me, nor did it explain how it verified identity beyond automated records. This failure raises concerns regarding compliance with the FCRAs requirement for reasonable investigations and accurate reporting. 

IV. ADMISSION OF INACCURATE CREDIT REPORTING In its response, Goldman Sachs Bank USA acknowledges that Equifax and TransUnion were not accurately reporting my bankruptcy during the investigation and that the Bank submitted update requests to those agencies. 

This admission confirms that inaccurate reporting occurred. Any period during which inaccurate, incomplete, or misleading information was furnished to consumer reporting agencies constitutes consumer harm, regardless of whether later corrections were requested. 

The Banks attempt to minimize this issue by stating that updates may take up to 30 days does not negate the fact that inaccurate information was furnished and persisted on my credit reports.

V. BANKRUPTCY DOES NOT OVERRIDE IDENTITY THEFT CLAIMS The Bank references a XXXX XXXX XXXX filing and asserts that collection efforts ceased upon notification. However, the presence of a bankruptcy filing does not resolve the underlying issue of whether the account itself was validly opened or authorized. 

Identity theft claims must be evaluated independently of bankruptcy status. Reporting obligations remain subject to FCRA requirements, and inaccurate reporting related to identity theft is unlawful regardless of bankruptcy proceedings. 

The Banks response does not address whether the account should have been reported at all once identity theft was asserted and documented. 

VI. LACK OF DOCUMENTARY EVIDENCE The Bank states that it is unable to provide additional information related to its investigation and that it can not provide signed documents because consent was electronic. This lack of documentation undermines the credibility of the Banks conclusions. 

If the Bank can not produce evidence demonstrating that I personally opened or authorized the account, it can not reasonably conclude that the account is mine. Assertions without evidence do not satisfy legal standards for investigation or reporting accuracy.

VII. PREVIOUS CFPB CASE CLOSURE AND NEW CASE INITIATION The Bank requested closure of CFPB complaint number XXXX, and that case was closed with explanation. However, closure of a CFPB complaint does not constitute a determination that the Banks actions were lawful or that the dispute has been resolved. 

Because the Bank failed to address the identity theft report, failed to provide evidence of authorization, and acknowledged inaccuracies in credit reporting, I am initiating a new CFPB complaint to ensure continued oversight and review of these unresolved issues.

Consumer complaint narrative: In XX/XX/XXXX, I took out an installment loan from Regional Finance Corporation of Texas at one of their XXXXarea branches. I borrowed {$7400.00}. Under the Truth in Lending Act and Regulation Z, a lender can leave credit insurance premiums out of the disclosed finance charge only when the coverage is truly optional, its cost is clearly disclosed, and the borrower signs off on it knowingly. None of that happened here. Treat those premiums as what they actually were, a cost of the credit, and the real rate on this loan runs well above the figure on the paperwork and above what Texas law permits a licensed lender to charge. The disclosures were not just incomplete. They were false. When I discovered this, I did what the fine print in Regional Finance 's own contract told me to do : I filed a consumer arbitration with the XXXX XXXX XXXX in XX/XX/XXXX. Regional Finance then missed its deadline to pay the required filing fees. The case was closed, and their payment showed up only after the fact. I agreed to move forward on the merits anyway. Their response was not to answer for the loan. Instead, their outside law firm filed a counterclaim against me, an individual consumer representing myself, which I can only understand as an attempt to make asserting my rights more expensive and frightening than giving up. I am one borrower. Regional Finance writes loans like mine across Texas every day, at storefronts serving people who can least afford to pay interest on insurance they never knew they bought. I am reporting this so the Commission has a record of how this company originates its loans and how it treats customers who push back. The arbitration remains pending.
