Consumer complaint narrative:
Between XX/XX/XXXX and XX/XX/XXXX, I authorized multiple student-loan payments through CRIs website totaling several XXXX dollars. 
Each attempt produced an on-screen confirmation and a Thank you for your payment email showing the payment amount, effective date, and account information ending in XXXX ( XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX 
Because these confirmations stated no further action is required, I reasonably believed the payments were processed. 

The XXXX Events On XX/XX/XXXX, CRI posted a message in my online portal titled Action Needed : Your previous payment could not be processed ( see Exhibit A ). 
After logging in and reviewing that notice, I immediately called CRIs customer-service line. 
The representative verified my account number and instructed me simply to resubmit the payment. 
At no point did CRI mention that my XXXX XXXX XXXXXXXX XXXX routing numberwhich I had successfully used for years, including under XXXXwas incompatible with their system. 
Following the representatives instructions, I resubmitted the payment using the same routing details. 

The Communication Failures CRI may argue that it issued additional portal messages or automated emails directing me to log in for updates. 
While I acknowledge those existed, they were generic, nonspecific, and inadequate for an issue as serious as a failed payment. 
No email or notice explicitly stated why the payment failed or that my account risked delinquency. 
Consequently, I continued to see active payment confirmations in my account and had no reason to believe the transactions hadnt cleared. 
By the time clearer delinquency letters appeared in XXXX, the account had already been reported XXXX, XXXX, and XXXX past due, resulting in an approximate XXXX credit score drop. 

XXXX XXXX and XXXX XXXX It was not until XXXX XXXXafter months of repeated payment attempts and callsthat a CRI representative finally disclosed the true reason : the routing number format, not the account number, was causing returns. 
Once this was explained, I immediately corrected the information and made a successful payment on XX/XX/XXXX, even though my account had already been placed into forbearance during the ongoing review. 

Response to CRIs Show Proof of Cleared Payment Claim CRIs repeated statement that no payments cleared our system mischaracterizes the dispute. 
My complaint is not that CRI accepted and reversed a paymentit is that their system confirmed receipt and provided no timely, clear notice that payments were being rejected before credit damage occurred. 
Consumers can not produce bank withdrawal proof for a transaction that never left the institution precisely because CRIs payment portal malfunctioned and failed to communicate it in real time. 
The on-screen and email confirmations constitute furnisher-originated documentation that the payment was properly initiated in good faith and that the servicers system, not the borrower, prevented completion. 

Summary : In XX/XX/XXXX my federally owned student loans were transferred from XXXX to CRI. Beginning in XX/XX/XXXX I made my monthly payments through CRIs official online portal using the same XXXX XXXX XXXXXXXX account and electronic routing format I have always used for other bills. Each time I submitted a payment, CRIs system generated a confirmation and visually accepted the payment, so I reasonably believed the payments had gone through. 

Later, in XX/XX/XXXX, CRI placed a message in my online portal inbox ( I have the screenshot ) saying : Your previous payment could not be processed. Please submit a new payment or apply for assistance. I did exactly what the notice told me to do : I called CRI. On that XXXX call, I was told only to re-verify my account number and resubmit the payment. I was not told the real and specific problem that CRI was rejecting my XXXX XXXX XXXXXXXX payment because of the routing format. If I had been told in XXXX, Your payments are failing because of the routing number format, use this routing number or pay by phone, I would have fixed it in XXXX. 

Instead, CRI kept accepting payment attempts in the portal, kept issuing confirmations, and kept showing me an account view that looked like the payment was received. I am attaching a screenshot from the portal that shows Last Payment Received : {$200.00} ( XX/XX/XXXX ) this is important because XXXX is now telling the CFPB that no payments were processed before XX/XX/XXXX, but their own portal represented to me that a payment was received on XX/XX/XXXX. That is exactly what I was relying on. 

In XX/XX/XXXX, when I called again, CRI finally explained the real issue that the payment attempts were getting bank return codes like Unable to Locate Account / Returned because of how the routing number was entered. The first time I heard that clear explanation was months after the first payment attempt and after the account had already rolled to 90 days late. As soon as I finally got the correct information in XXXX, I updated the payment information and made the payment even though the account was in forbearance. That shows I was able and willing to pay ; I just wasnt given the right instruction early enough. 

After my CFPB complaints on XX/XX/XXXX ( against CRI, XXXX, and XXXX ) and XX/XX/XXXX ( follow-up ), CRI responded XXXX. Both of their XXXX responses repeat the same point : they say the payments were initiated but did not clear, so they consider the XXXX reporting to be accurate. They also keep saying, If you can show us that the bank actually sent the money, we will review. The problem with that position is : CRIs own system was the one accepting the payments and issuing confirmations. 

CRIs XXXX XXXX and phone agent did not tell me the real, specific fix ( routing format ). 

CRIs portal later showed XXXX XXXX Received : {$200.00} ( XX/XX/XXXX ), which is inconsistent with their claim to CFPB that nothing was processed. 

By the time they finally explained the real reason in XXXX, the account had already hit 90 days late ( see their XX/XX/XXXX letter in my portal ). 

I then fixed it immediately. 

So, this is not a case of me refusing to pay or not having funds it is a servicer-created, servicer-prolonged payment-processing failure that CRI then used to justify negative credit reporting. 

I also understand CRI may point to the fact that they sent me generic check your portal emails ( I found the XX/XX/XXXX email in my regular email, the one that tells you to log in to see important information ). I am acknowledging that. But even when I followed up in XXXX, the agent did not tell me Your routing number is the issue. That missing piece of information is why the problem kept repeating and why the account aged into delinquency. 

Finally, I have multiple related CFPB complaints on file from XX/XX/XXXX ( against CRI, XXXX and XXXX  ) and XX/XX/XXXX ( CRI again ). I am providing these so the CFPB can see this is an ongoing dispute about accuracy of reporting after a processing failure not a request for a goodwill deletion.

No bureau may continue reporting information that can not be verified with documented evidence from the original creditor.

The accounts in question include late payments, charge-offs, collections, and unauthorized inquiries. I demand deletion because : None of the furnishers have produced a legally binding contract, original signed agreement, or complete chain of title proving assignment or ownership of the alleged debts. Without such documentation, continued reporting violates FCRA 609 ( a ) ( 1 ), FCRA 611 ( a ) ( 5 ), and 15 U.S.C. 1681e ( b ), which require accurate and complete reporting.

Debt collectors must prove ownership and legal right to collect by producing the bill of sale and assignment chain referencing my name and account number. Bulk sales without individualized documentation do not satisfy the law. Failure to provide this is a violation of FDCPA, 15 U.S.C. 1692g ( b ), as well as FCRA 623 ( a ) ( 3 ) requiring accurate reporting by furnishers.

No section of the FCRA explicitly defines charge-off, and furnishers routinely misuse this label in violation of Generally Accepted Accounting Principles ( GAAP ) and FFIEC guidelines. Reporting a balance after charging off is deceptive, and without complete accounting ledgers, amortization schedules, and records of principal/interest allocation, the data remains unverifiable and misleading under FCRA 607 ( b ).

Late payments are not permitted to be reported indefinitely, and in many cases, lenders fail to comply with 15 U.S.C. 1666 ( b ) ( billing error protections ) and Regulation Z ( Truth in Lending Act ), which requires proper notice and opportunity to cure before declaring delinquency. Failure to produce payment histories proving their claims makes this reporting unlawful.

Hard inquiries made without my written authorization or permissible purpose violate FCRA 604 ( a ) ( 2 ). Any inquiry not tied to a firm offer of credit or an account I expressly applied for must be deleted.

Further, I invoke my rights under the Uniform Commercial Code ( UCC 3-501, UCC 3-505 ) regarding proper presentment and proof of claim, none of which have been satisfied by furnishers. Without full validation, any continued reporting constitutes willful noncompliance under FCRA 616617, subjecting both XXXX XXXX XXXX and the furnishers to liability.

Consumer complaint narrative: I am submitting this complaint regarding the continued reporting, furnishing, publication, processing, and verification of inaccurate, incomplete, misleading, unverifiable, and legally noncompliant information on my consumer report. The conduct described herein constitutes violations of the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( 15 U.S.C. 1681 et seq. ), including but not limited to FCRA 602, 604, 607 ( a ), 607 ( b ), 611, 623 ( a ) ( 1 ) ( A ), 623 ( a ) ( 1 ) ( B ), 623 ( a ) ( 2 ), 623 ( a ) ( 8 ), 623 ( b ), 605B, and all applicable federal consumer protection requirements. The furnisher and/or consumer reporting agency has failed to maintain reasonable procedures to assure maximum possible accuracy as required by FCRA 607 ( b ), failed to conduct a lawful and reasonable reinvestigation under FCRA 611 ( a ), failed to review all relevant information submitted by the consumer, failed to properly identify the source and method of verification, failed to provide competent evidence supporting the continued reporting of the disputed information, and continued to publish information that is inaccurate, misleading, incomplete, and damaging. The continued reporting of disputed information without competent documentary evidence raises serious concerns regarding compliance with FCRA 607 and 611, the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act where applicable, the Consumer Financial Protection Act, and all related federal and state consumer protection statutes. Upon information and belief, the furnisher and/or consumer reporting agency has engaged in automated, superficial, and legally deficient dispute processing practices rather than conducting the reasonable investigation required by law. The reporting of information that can not be fully verified through original business records, account-level documentation, complete payment history records, signed contracts, and competent evidentiary support is unlawful and must cease immediately. The burden of accuracy rests upon the reporting entity and not upon the consumer. Any representation that disputed information has been verified without providing a lawful basis for such verification is insufficient under the FCRA. Furthermore, any failure to correct, delete, suppress, or block inaccurate information after receiving notice of dispute constitutes continued publication of potentially false information and exposes the responsible parties to liability for negligent and willful noncompliance under FCRA 616 and 617. The continued reporting of inaccurate information causes substantial harm, including damage to reputation, loss of credit opportunities, higher interest rates, denial of housing opportunities, emotional distress, and financial injury. I demand a complete CFPB-supervised investigation, disclosure of all procedures used to verify the disputed information, identification of every party involved in the verification process, disclosure of the date and method of verification, disclosure of all records relied upon during the investigation, and immediate deletion of any information that can not be fully substantiated through competent documentary evidence. If the information can not be verified in strict compliance with federal law, it must be permanently deleted and removed from all consumer reporting databases. I further request that the CFPB require the responsible entities to fully comply with all obligations imposed under the Fair Credit Reporting Act, the Consumer Financial Protection Act, and all applicable federal and state consumer protection laws and regulations. The only acceptable resolution is the immediate deletion, correction, suppression, or permanent removal of all inaccurate, incomplete, misleading, unverifiable, or unlawfully reported information and full compliance with all consumer protection requirements.

During this interaction, it was disclosed that no meaningful notes had been entered in the case file documenting prior calls or the substance of the dispute, despite multiple earlier contacts and the existence of Kia Customer Care file numbers XXXX and XXXX.

Why This Is a Compliance Issue Buyer designation requires affirmative consent and signature.

Lessee or primary account holder status does not confer purchase authority.

Kia Finance can not identify any document bearing my signature agreeing to purchase the vehicle.

The incorrect buyer designation is a seller-side documentation error.

Kia Finance has refused to issue or coordinate corrective documentation.

As a result, the purchaser has suffered financial harm due to title delay and increased interest charges, and Kia Finance has effectively attempted to shift liability to a non-purchasing party.

Resolution Requested I am requesting that Kia Finance America : 1. Issue or coordinate seller-side corrective documentation, such as a corrected Bill of Sale or seller error correction affidavit, confirming that I am not a buyer and that my name was included in error.

2. Provide written confirmation allowing the North Carolina DMV and the lender to complete proper title issuance and lien perfection.

The stress and frustration caused by this misinformation is unacceptable and further underscores the need for enforcement action to prevent deceptive advertising practices.

Sub-issue: Deficiency balance after repossession
Consumer complaint narrative: In XX/XX/XXXX I financed a XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX through this lender. The retail installment contract expressly states it is governed by Arizona law. In XX/XX/XXXX I verbally requested the lender cease and desist contact on this account. The vehicle was then repossessed on XX/XX/XXXX and sold at a disposition on XX/XX/XXXX. The lender claims a resulting deficiency of approximately {$9000.00}, now reported on my credit file as a charged-off balance. Under Arizona law ( A.R.S. 47-9611 and 47-9614 ), before disposing of repossessed collateral the secured party must send the debtor a pre-sale notice of disposition. I never received any such notice before the XX/XX/XXXX sale. When I asked the lender about this, a representative indicated the notice was not sent and pointed to my cease and desist request as the reason. That is not a lawful excuse : a cease and desist limits collection communications only it does not suspend the lender 's independent statutory duty under 47-9611/47-9614 to send a disposition notice before sale. The lender 's reliance on my cease and desist to justify not sending the notice is itself an admission the required notice was never sent. The lender was also required under A.R.S. 47-9616 to send a post-sale explanation of how the deficiency was calculated. I never received that either. I attempted to obtain these documents directly. I gave the lender verbal authorization to lift the cease and desist for the limited purpose of email communication to my email address the same verbal method by which the cease and desist was originally placed. The lender refused to accept my verbal authorization to send me documents, while continuing to treat the cease and desist as valid against me. This asymmetric application honoring a verbal instruction when it lets the lender withhold required documents, but rejecting a verbal instruction when it would require the lender to provide them is an unfair and abusive practice and a deliberate barrier to my consumer rights.
